name: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
problem: KV cache activations become the dominant memory consumer at long context, and existing solutions fail to represent them accurately below 4 bits.
mechanism: Four components: (1) PER-CHANNEL key quantization - change the dimension along which keys are quantized to match their distribution; (2) PRE-RoPE key quantization - quantize keys BEFORE the rotary positional embedding, so RoPE's per-position rotation cannot smear values across quantization buckets; (3) non-uniform, per-layer sensitivity-weighted datatypes so each layer gets the codebook that suits it; (4) per-vector dense-and-sparse decomposition isolating outliers for each vector rather than globally.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): on LLaMA / Llama-2 / Llama-3 / Mistral, LESS THAN 0.1 PERPLEXITY DEGRADATION with 3-bit quantization on both WikiText-2 and C4, outperforming existing approaches. COMPRESSION RATIO: 3-bit KV cache vs FP16 KV cache = ~5.3x cache reduction. Consequence claim: enables serving LLaMA-7B at up to 1 MILLION context on a SINGLE A100-80GB, and up to 10 million context across 8 A100-80GBs. QUALITY COST: <0.1 perplexity - the <0.1 figure is the headline and it is unusually strong.
